subject: biology
title: Photosynthesis
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Photosynthesis — AQA GCSE Biology (8461) specification, section 4.4.1.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology (AQA) practice covering Photosynthesis, specification section 4.4.1.
final_note: You worked through Photosynthesis — 12 specification statements.

concepts.def: The reaction represented by the equation carbon dioxide + water → (light) glucose + oxygen, which takes place in the chloroplasts. Written with chemical symbols, CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and O2.
A reaction that takes in energy from its surroundings. Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction in which energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.
The amount of product formed in a given time, calculated by dividing the amount of product by the time taken, for example bubbles of oxygen released per minute or cm3 of oxygen produced per minute.

The factor that is controlling the rate of photosynthesis at that moment, so that increasing it increases the rate. Temperature, light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and the amount of chlorophyll all affect the rate of photosynthesis.

Temperature, light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and the amount of chlorophyll interact, and any one of them may be the factor that limits photosynthesis. On a graph, the limiting factor is the one which, when increased on its own, raises the rate further.

concepts.term: inverse square law and light intensity
concepts.def: Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the light source. Doubling the distance reduces the light intensity to one quarter, and halving the distance increases it four times.

Growers enhance temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration in greenhouses to gain the maximum rate of photosynthesis. The cost of enhancing the conditions must be less than the extra income gained, so limiting factors are important in the economics of greenhouse growing.

The glucose produced in photosynthesis may be used for respiration, converted into insoluble starch for storage, used to produce fat or oil for storage, used to produce cellulose which strengthens the cell wall, or used to produce amino acids for protein synthesis.
Ions that are absorbed from the soil and used by plants, together with the glucose produced in photosynthesis, to produce amino acids for protein synthesis.

mcqs.q: Which line shows the equation for photosynthesis written in chemical symbols?
options: CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and O2.
C6H12O6 and O2 react to form CO2 and H2O.
CO2 and O2 react to form C6H12O6 and H2O.
CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and heat.
mcqs.explain: This is the equation carbon dioxide + water → (light) glucose + oxygen written with the chemical symbols CO2, H2O, C6H12O6 and O2.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction?
options: Energy is transferred from the chloroplasts to the surroundings.
Energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts.
Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the mitochondria.
Energy is transferred from the glucose to the environment as heat.
mcqs.explain: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction in which energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.

mcqs.q: A student measures the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed by counting bubbles of oxygen. She counts 90 bubbles in 3 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis?
options: 30 bubbles per minute
90 bubbles per minute
270 bubbles per minute
0.03 bubbles per minute
mcqs.explain: Rate is the amount of product divided by the time taken: 90 bubbles ÷ 3 minutes = 30 bubbles per minute.

mcqs.q: A student plots the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed against light intensity at a constant temperature. The graph rises steeply and then becomes a horizontal line. Which statement explains the horizontal part of the graph?
options: Light intensity is still limiting the rate on the flat part.
The plant has switched from photosynthesis to respiration.
The rate is still rising but the graph is not showing it.
Another factor, such as temperature, is now limiting the rate.
mcqs.explain: The factors interact and any one of them may be the factor that limits photosynthesis. Once light intensity is no longer limiting, temperature or carbon dioxide concentration limits the rate, so the rate stops rising.

mcqs.q: A graph shows the rate of photosynthesis against light intensity at 20 °C and at 30 °C, both at the same carbon dioxide concentration. Both curves rise and then become horizontal, but the 30 °C curve becomes horizontal at a higher rate. Which statement about the graph is correct?
options: Light intensity is limiting the rate where the 20 °C curve is flat.
Temperature is limiting the rate on the steep part of each curve.
Temperature is limiting the rate where the 20 °C curve is flat.
Raising the temperature to 50 °C would raise the flat part again.
mcqs.explain: On the flat part, increasing light intensity has no effect, but raising the temperature to 30 °C gives a higher rate. The factor that raises the rate when it alone is increased is the limiting factor.

mcqs.q: A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 20 cm from a piece of pondweed. Light intensity is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the lamp. What happens to the light intensity reaching the pondweed?
options: It falls to 1/2 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/16 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/4 of the intensity at 10 cm.
It falls to 1/20 of the intensity at 10 cm.
mcqs.explain: The distance is doubled, so the light intensity falls by a factor of 2 squared: it becomes one quarter of the intensity at 10 cm.

mcqs.q: How does a plant obtain the amino acids it uses for protein synthesis?
options: Amino acids are made from starch and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are made from glucose and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are absorbed from the soil by the roots.
Proteins are absorbed from the soil by the roots.
mcqs.explain: Glucose produced in photosynthesis is used to produce amino acids, and to do this plants also use nitrate ions that are absorbed from the soil.
